page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.3xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server instance belonging to the ecs.se1ne family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance features 12 dedicated physical cores and 12 vCPUs, indicating a one-to-one mapping of physical cores to virtual CPUs with hyper-threading disabled or configured for single-thread-per-core execution. It is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates on a KVM hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics are generally low, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% categories, respectively. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression also demonstrate poor throughput. Conversely, multi-core execution scales to average levels, as shown by stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU scores, which all rank in the middle 50% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth remains stable at average levels, measuring 59.2 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 49.35 GB/sec for large-block write operations, though the PassMark memory score itself is relatively weak.

Given its hardware profile and performance characteristics, the ecs.se1ne.3xlarge is suited for memory-intensive workloads that benefit from a high RAM-to-vCPU ratio but do not require high single-threaded CPU performance. Suitable applications include database operations, as reflected in its average PassMark database score and Redis SET performance of 8.48 million operations per second. It is also capable of handling moderate multi-threaded tasks such as software compilation and basic text or image processing. However, the lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, and the 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth may limit data-transfer-heavy applications.
